observations: Contract v5 uses root-minted send-only notifications for guest queue kicks and RX wakeups. Attachment remains an endpoint Call.
The receive-loop tests passed for a pending network wake with a stale IPC tag and for combined network, block and serial wake bits, without an RPC, fault callback or reply.
The real packet-path host test passed through the updated notification boundary, canonical queues and x86 IOAPIC adapter.
The full target gate passed ARM network, block and console I/O. Boot logs identify net_virt contract v5 and successful hardware-backed attachment.
limitations: Coalescing tests mock the receive boundary; no claim is made that all wake combinations were forced on target.
The NIC driver's RX endpoint events are unchanged. Intel NIC integration and firmware network PD wiring remain outstanding.
The Intel network receive path is not yet qualified; x86 link and host packet tests are not target network evidence.
Canonical integration, Debian, GUI and v0.4 release remain incomplete.
